title: Wet-felted Christmas bauble set
subtitle: Six solid merino spheres felted over balloon forms, about 6 cm each
excerpt: Wet-felt six merino baubles over inflated round balloons, remove the balloons, and hang them from ribbon loops. The baubles are solid-coloured or layered, about 6 cm across when fulled. The process is reliable once you understand the resist principle.
sourceNotes: Synthesised from traditional wet-felting practice. Balloon resist forms for spherical vessels are a standard modern wet-felting technique used widely in guild workshops.

glossaryTerms.definition: A felting method using hot soapy water and agitation to lock wool fibres together. The fibres shrink and matt as they are rubbed and rolled.
An object or template placed inside or against wet-felted roving to hold a shape during the felting process. Removed when the felt is firm enough to hold the shape alone.
The later, more vigorous stage of wet felting where the felt has formed and is worked harder to shrink and firm it to final dimensions.

locks it into a sphere, then the balloon is burst and removed. The finished baubles are about 6 cm across. Make a set of six in coordinating colours. The
stage determines the final size; stop fulling when the felt is firm and the desired diameter is reached.

items.name: Olive-oil soap dissolved in hot water (sudsy water)
Ribbon or thread for hanging loops

content.text: Inflate six balloons to approximately 6 cm in diameter. Tie them off. Consistent inflation produces consistent finished baubles; use a ruler to check each balloon is roughly the same size.

Pull thin wisps of roving and lay them over the balloon in a single cross-hatch layer, alternating horizontal and vertical passes. Cover the balloon completely, including the knot end. Apply two full cross-hatch layers for each bauble. Wetting down the first layer before applying the second helps the layers grip the balloon surface and hold their position.

Pour warm soapy water over the balloon and roving, covering the surface completely. Support the balloon in one hand and rub gently with the other, turning the balloon so all surfaces are rubbed evenly. Rub for at least five minutes per bauble before pressing more firmly. The roving will begin to shrink and tighten around the balloon. If the roving slides under rubbing, let it rest for two minutes and try again with lighter pressure.

Once the surface feels cohesive and the fibres no longer separate under pressure, roll each bauble across the bamboo mat under your palm, increasing pressure gradually. Alternate between hot and cold water rinses to shock the fibres. Full until the felt is firm and bounces back slightly when pressed. This usually takes 10 to 15 minutes of rolling.
Step 5: Remove the balloons and finish

Once the felt is firm, burst each balloon with a pin through the roving near the knot. Ease the deflated balloon out through the hole. Pinch the opening closed and felt the hole shut by adding a small amount of roving and needling it over the gap if needed, or wet-felt it by rubbing the area with soapy fingers. Rinse each bauble thoroughly in cool water, shape by hand, and dry on a rack. Thread ribbon through the top when dry.

items.problem: The roving slid around the balloon before it felted
items.cause: The roving layer was too thick to grip the balloon surface, or the rubbing started before the surface was fully wet
items.fix: Wet the first roving layer fully before adding the second layer; thin roving layers grip better than thick ones. Also try pulling the roving into finer wisps.

items.problem: The bauble came out lumpy rather than spherical
items.cause: Uneven roving coverage, or uneven pressure during rubbing; one side was rubbed more than the other
items.fix: Check roving coverage before wetting down. Rotate the balloon steadily during rubbing and spend equal time on all surfaces.
